tasks.gr11-developing-economies-poverty-t3: Topic: Developing economies and poverty. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover the characteristics distinguishing developing from developed economies (low per capita income, high population growth, low industrialisation, dependence on primary commodities, weak institutions). Define absolute poverty (income below poverty line) and relative poverty. Explain the Human Development Index (HDI): life expectancy, education and income dimensions. Analyse causes of poverty in SA (unemployment, inequality, apartheid legacy) and government interventions (social grants, RDP housing, EPWP, free basic services).
tasks.gr11-money-banking-t3: Topic: Money, banking and the central bank. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover the six functions of money (medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account, standard of deferred payment, measure of value, standard of value) and forms of money (commodity, representative, fiat/token). Commercial banks accept deposits, grant credit, transfer funds, create credit. The South African Reserve Bank (SARB): banker to government, banker to commercial banks, lender of last resort, custodian of foreign reserves, monetary policy via the repo rate. Explain how repo rate changes affect borrowing, spending and inflation.
tasks.gr11-micro-lending-t3: Topic: Micro-lending and financial inclusion. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover micro-lending as the provision of small loans to low-income individuals and SMMEs who lack access to formal bank credit. Institutions: Small Enterprise Finance Agency (SEFA), Khula Enterprise Finance, community-based rotating savings (stokvels). The Grameen Bank model of group lending. National Credit Act (NCA) provisions to protect consumers from reckless lending. Problems: high interest rates, over-indebtedness, exploitation. Evaluate micro-lending as a poverty alleviation and entrepreneurship development tool in SA.
tasks.gr11-south-africa-africa-t3: Topic: South Africa in Africa — SADC and NEPAD. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover SA's economic dominance in the Southern African region (GDP, trade, investment, infrastructure). Southern African Development Community (SADC): founded 1992, 16 member states, objectives (regional integration, peace, development), achievements and challenges. New Partnership for Africa's Development (NEPAD): 2001, based on African ownership, peer review mechanism (APRM), infrastructure, governance. African Union (AU). SA in BRICS. Evaluate whether regional integration promotes development for participating states.
